notes:
Prospect profile: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics) with ~300 engs. Started on Redwood Hosted API to validate dev experience. Now moving to Dedicated evaluation for predictable SLOs and data isolation. Short, choppy CRM notes below:
- PM quote: 'we need predictable latency during peak import windows; we can't have tail spikes break sessions.'
- Primary drivers: latency stability, cost predictability, security controls (VPC/KMS/retention), and routing fallback to avoid outages.
- Use-case specifics: in-app chat assistant (95% of traffic), embeddings-driven doc-search for product help, reranking for UI recommendations.
- Traffic profile: steady ~50 req/s for chat, bursts to 200 req/s during release days. Req size mostly short contexts (avg 250 tokens), some long-history queries for power users.
- Model preference: prefer open/quantized variants; want Redwood to recommend quantization profiles. Interested in small-medium model family for cost; willing to trial larger for quality-sensitive flows.
- Security ask: SSO/SAML + audit logs + EU data residency for EU customers, KMS integration.
- Buying process: procurement + security team must sign off; legal expects SOC2 docs and a 3rd party penetration test summary.
- Sales angle so far: emphasize predictable latency (Dedicated), routing fallbacks, canary rollouts, and cost-optimization via batching.
- Customer sentiment: curious but cautious on ops overhead; likes Redwood console telemetry screenshots.
poc_plan: 6-week Dedicated POC. Phase 1 (week 0-2): Quick Dedicated spin-up in customer's VPC via partner region; deploy sample model variant (quantized medium) and mirror 10% traffic via edge routing from hosted -> dedicated (canary). Phase 2 (week 3-4): Scale to 50% traffic, run regression evals and cost telemetry; enable KV/prefix caching. Phase 3 (week 5-6): Full load test (200 rps burst), enable region failover test (eu -> na), finalize rollback and SLO docs. Canary policy: start at 10% traffic -> 30% -> 50% with 24h obser windows. Fallbacks: automatic fallback to Hosted API variant + lower-cost quantized model if: increased error rate (5xx raise > 2x baseline), p95 latency > 2x baseline, or QoR regression on eval set. Rollback policy: automated rollback on SLO breach or manual rollback via console; keep config history and tag canary releases. Dev infra: VPC peering, private subnet, KMS integration, and optional on-prem connector for sensitive EU subset.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for chat under Dedicated POC <= 350ms (measured at edge)
99.9% availability for POC window (excluding planned tests)
No QoR regression > 2% on reference prompt set for critical intents (support/escalation)
Cost target: estimated token-unit cost reduction >= 20% vs hosted burst pricing for equivalent throughput
Security: KMS integration validated, SSO login flow tested, audit logs delivered to customer SIEM
pricing_concerns: Customer is cost-aware. Wants committed Reserved pricing tier with burst credits. Asking for blended ARR estimate for 12-month commit and a delta vs pure-hosted spend. Procurement will push for a capped overage model.
sales_playbook_notes: Position Dedicated as predictable SLO + data isolation product; lead with canary + fallback plan. Provide a sample TCO model (Diego to produce) showing batching/quantization savings. Offer a pilot contract (6 weeks) + PO terms that allow easy rollbacks to Hosted in case performance/cost goals not met.
other_notes: Requested a short runbook for ops: how to promote canary -> prod, how to inspect token-cost breakdown per route. They also asked for an example A/B rollout for model variants. Jira tickets created for onboarding tasks: INF-1429 (infra), SEC-87 (security docs).
